implementation.preserved: Factories/signatures, client ID/context synchronization, central/ordinary launch arguments and seed order, edge shared loop with no new periodic task, explicit spawn policy, os._exit, training/transport/aggregation semantics and normal process cleanup.

iterations: Corrected a temporary indentation error before authoritative green checks.
Corrected test assumptions about logical versus spawned client IDs and TCP TIME_WAIT. Actual 2/6 reports and logical-ID mapping remain mandatory.
Opened the fallback async generator inside a running task so asyncio registers its finalizer, rather than constructing its first asend outside async-generator hooks.

Renamed the server close-hook marker to server_close_started. A failed/stalled client can trigger that hook and server exit code zero without aggregation; the stalled test instead requires no aggregate and only one actual processed payload. An aggregation-time callback cannot observe a partially received round, so the stalled server uses an observational wrapper of the actual payload completion handler, preserving decoding and processing.
After the close-hook correction reran the affected positive/stalled socket checks and all required teardown negatives; unaffected broad/cooperative checks were retained.

ci_handoff.combined_run_note: 47-case development runs had three harness assertion/setup failures later repaired; durations are observations, not green completion claims. Final 48 unique cases pass via retained cooperative and fresh teardown/socket partitions.
ci_handoff.budget_advice: Five minutes is insufficient for one sequential combined startup suite. Register the two markers and use measured partition durations plus host/CI margin, or a larger bounded combined step. Preserve all five negative cases and their 30/90+5+5 second subprocess bounds. Linux CI durations remain to be measured by 1C.

limitations: Natural cleanup relies on cooperative extension code. Runner/run_app cancellation gathering and async-generator finalization can stall; Runner executor wait can reach 300 seconds. The fallback executor timeout only bounds its wait and cannot kill a running thread.

Watchdog exits are expected containment only for negative tests. They prove neither graceful Python finalization nor original exception delivery. The real aiohttp stall required TERM then KILL; stalled sockets can leave a child alive after server exit code zero.

Production os._exit in successful rounds proves transport/training/aggregation and normal process disappearance, not Python finally execution. Returning/signal/error bootstrap tests independently validate loop cleanup.

PID/start-time identities track owned groups and durable child-start markers. Direct subprocess children are waited/reaped; zombie descendants are already exited and cannot be reaped by a non-parent harness. No live owned survivor is allowed.

Three existing Nanochat tests skip for absent native rustbpe/nanochat source prerequisites. Git submodules are not initialized in this isolated worktree. This suite is not full Nanochat, ViT, robotics, MLX or Linux support qualification.
Eight existing multiprocess fork warnings remain in each full existing suite and are assigned to Phase 1C.
No general lifecycle framework, new production child supervision, manifest/lock/default-Python change, push or nested agent work was introduced.
